messages:
sophie-support: heads-up — acme-inc reporting lots of 504s and timeouts hitting /v1/generate since ~2024-10-11 11:05 UTC. customer says it started after a traffic spike. :rotating_light:

sophie-support: sample failed response header: 
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
Date: Fri, 11 Oct 2024 11:06:02 GMT
X-Request-ID: rq_7f8b2c3d

sophie-support: quick repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-3b","prompt":"<long customer prompt>"}'
```

jamal-runtime: thx. grabbing traces for rq_7f8b2c3d and querying our queue metrics for tenant=acme-inc now.

jamal-runtime: metrics snapshot (ingress -> continuous batcher):
```
continuous_batcher_queue_depth{tenant="acme-inc"} 512
continuous_batcher_dequeue_rate{tenant="acme-inc"} 5 requests/s
gateway_request_queue_depth_total 10240
gateway_request_queue_limit_per_tenant 512
request_queue_timeouts{tenant="acme-inc"} 118
```
(look at the queue depth = 512 — that's the per-tenant hard cap)

maria-sre: seeing same in infra dashboards — host pool load ~94%, one batcher group cbatch-7 showing a backlog of ~480 queued requests with p99 dequeue latency > 12s. p50 is fine.

jamal-runtime: root cause hypothesis: continuous-batching backlog + long-running model seqs -> KV cache warmups causing batcher to hold slots for many seconds. requests pile until per-tenant queue cap hits and gateway starts returning queue timeout 504s.

jamal-runtime: quick mitigation options (pick 1-2):
- emergency fallback: route tenant -> smaller model variant (shorter seq, less KV warmup).
- temporary tenant rate-limit (throttle) while backlog drains.
- bump per-tenant queue depth (risky for noisy neighbors).
- restart affected batcher group to clear stuck KV warmups (disruptive).

chris-cs: customer approved temporary fallback + rate cap. they prefer not to restart infra if possible. priority is to restore success rate.

sophie-support: can we do routing + rate limit now? please confirm exact commands.

jamal-runtime: executing steps:
1) create tenant-routing override: acme-inc -> model=redwood-small-1 (canary)
2) apply tenant rate-limit: acme-inc max_rps=20
3) monitor continuous_batcher_queue_depth and dequeue latency

rook-deploy-bot: tenant-routing change submitted: `tenant-routing/overrides/acme-inc` -> model=redwood-small-1 (canary) at 1717654360. status: in_progress

rook-deploy-bot: rate-limit policy applied: `rl/tenant/acme-inc` max_rps=20 at 1717654362. status: success

maria-sre: I also kicked a soft restart of cbatch-7 (graceful drains) at 1717654372: `kubectl -n runtime rollout restart sts/cbatch-7` — pods came back and began accepting new batches.

jamal-runtime: post-mitigation metrics ~5 minutes later:
```
continuous_batcher_queue_depth{tenant="acme-inc"} 45
continuous_batcher_dequeue_rate{tenant="acme-inc"} 18 requests/s
request_queue_timeouts{tenant="acme-inc"} 2
p99_gateway_latency{tenant="acme-inc"} 1.2s
```

ingress-monitor-bot: alert cleared for acme-inc queue depth at 1717654386 — previous alert window resolved.

sophie-support: customer confirmed reduced 504s and acceptable UX on fallback model. they want longer-term fix (model tuning or capacity) — CS will follow up.

chris-cs: noted. filing a post-incident action: evaluate KV cache warmup mitigations, adjust per-tenant soft limits, and add auto-fallback runbook.

jamal-runtime: runbook items I'll add:
- detect continuous_batcher_queue_depth > 75% sustained for 3m -> auto-enable fallback to small model + alert to SRE/CS.
- instrument per-tenant tail-latency heatmap and KV warmup counts.
- consider adaptive per-tenant burst buffers instead of hard cap.

sophie-support: closing thread — reopening if anything regresses. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
